The variables of carbon exchange between land and atmosphere (i.e. gpp, npp, rh, and ra) allow us to link the biases in productivity with changes in phenology (e.g. Li et al., 2023, [10.22541/essoar.168298711.15374345/v1](https://doi.org/10.22541/essoar.168298711.15374345/v1)). Finally, the landCoverFrac variable provides the relative influence of each vegetation type on the total grid cell.
recuxg4k9Cb5JnXXm.Justification of Resources: To realistically simulate terrestrial ecosystem processes and land-atmosphere carbon, energy, and water exchanges, it is crucial that the seasonality and trend of plant phenology are correctly captured by the Earth system models. This opportunity delineates a set of variables and experiments needed to expand our understanding of model weaknesses and strengths.

recvvOPoRyfKPggGz.Description:
This opportunity will allow assessments in the fields of glaciology and glacio-hydrology across timescales in the past, present, and future. It focuses on glaciers in the polar regions (including peripheral glaciers in Greenland and (Sub-)Antarctica that are decoupled from the ice sheets) and mountain glaciers, as identified in the Randolph Glacier Inventory (RGI). 
 
These glaciers have been the largest cryospheric driver of sea-level rise in the 20th century. Depending on the scenario (AR6), glaciers are expected to remain the primary drivers of sea-level rise during the 21st century, exceeding the contributions from the two ice sheets. They have significance in sustaining ecosystems, modulating regional hydroclimates, and as a freshwater resource (particularly in, but not limited to, seasonally arid regions like central Asia and the western slopes of the Andes). Through feedbacks in the mass balance response to climate change, glaciers are regional-scale tipping points in the Earth system and are an important element in assessing geohazards (e.g., glacial lake outburst floods, avalanches).
recvvOPoRyfKPggGz.Expected Impacts:
(1) One important use case is the Glacier Model Intercomparison Project (GlacierMIP, under the umbrella of the WCRP CliC project), which is a coordinated intercomparison effort of global-scale glacier models aiming for model improvements and reducing uncertainties in global glacier projections. These involve historical and future simulations of glacier geometry change at century scales. The outputs from GlacierMIP have informed the IPCC Special Report on The Cryosphere and the Oceans in a Warming Climate (Hock et al. 2019) and IPCC AR6 report (Marzeion et al. 2020).
(2) Another use is integration of glacier melt in hydrologic models for accurate partitioning between glacier-melt, snow-melt, and baseflow contributions to runoff. This requires variables from terrestrial hydrology and snow processes at daily resolutions for sub-seasonal and seasonal assessments of streamflows.
(3) This opportunity will assist in the evaluation of the mountain cryosphere, with a particular emphasis on glaciers as important regional tipping points, which is a focus area of the WCRP CliC project. 
(4) The opportunity will further support assessments on local to regional-scale geohazards associated with glacier change under different scenarios, including glacial lake outburst floods, slope failures, avalanches and ice falls, etc.
recvvOPoRyfKPggGz.Justification of Resources: The variables in this opportunity are critical as inputs for the glacier modeling community and to study the impacts of climate change on glaciers and of glacier changes on climate systems.

recw4aPxilSdJZoJi.Description: The CMIP Panel agreed on providing a Rapid Evaluation Framework (REF) for new simulations that become available from upcoming CMIP phases. The idea is to evaluate and benchmark the newly available simulations as soon as they are uploaded to ESGF with metrics and diagnostics that are available through different open-source evaluation and benchmarking tools. The REF is envisioned to be available already for the Fast Track simulations, however, the available metrics and diagnostics will be limited to a temporal resolution of monthly mean data and a community selection of of about five metrics/diagnostics per realm. Results will be publicly displayed for the community to see.
recw4aPxilSdJZoJi.Expected Impacts: The suggested metrics/diagnostics for the REF to be available for the Fast Track simulations are in a first instance very basic evaluations and are not expected to require very specific variables. However, the impact of the publicly available evaluation and benchmarking results should be big since the community can get a quick overview of available simulations and their characteristics that might be interesting for different applications and analyses.
recw4aPxilSdJZoJi.Justification of Resources: This opportunity does not ask for additional variables or experiments. In the contrary, it will make use of the already proposed experiments and will provide an overview of the characteristics of the simulations of these experiments (e.g. Fast Track).
recw4aPxilSdJZoJi.Technical Notes: For any groups with comments on the diagnostics included in the variable groups, please consider responding to the survey which closes on the 18th September -these variables are indicative as the consultation is still open. https://wcrp-cmip.org/have-your-say-diagnostics-and-reference-data-for-the-ar7-fast-track/

recx5BaDZeGHHF1ek.Description: We currently have an inability of directly comparing models (simplified versions of the Earth system) and observations (complicated!). It would be great if we can collect "energy budget" terms across the realms (ocean, land, cryosphere, atmosphere) in a coherent way, so we can most appropriately "close" (or more correctly approximate) energy budget changes in a model that can be contrasted to observations
recx5BaDZeGHHF1ek.Expected Impacts: Having high-level energy budget metrics would be an ideal way of catching problem simulations that may have a very large imbalance that should be considered when interpreting projected fields (e.g. surface air temperature changes, and all the downstream changes that a larger/smaller warming would have on the climate system)
recx5BaDZeGHHF1ek.Justification of Resources: Having energy budget metrics would provide very helpful overview insights that would aid assessing fitness for purpose across numerous downstream uses. It would be possible to capture these metrics in a compact (small storage footprint form), however, these would be most useful in the case that spatially complete fields were saved (potentially through timeslice sums, e.g. decadal sum/average) which allows interpretation of energy flows, and changes to these through the full length of a simulation (e.g. 1850-2022) for historical.

recxXfc0Cj4ft3dRi.Description: Several components of the Earth system are highly susceptible to reaching a critical threshold – a tipping point – beyond which amplifying feedbacks can result in abrupt and/or irreversible changes in response to anthropogenic climate change. Crossing a tipping point can lead the systems to transition to an alternative state, often with reduced resilience to perturbations and recovery. Once triggered, the tipping of one of these elements can have far-reaching impacts on the global climate, ecosystems and humankind. Recent assessments have highlighted the increasing risk for potential tipping, in particular beyond 1.5°C global warming, and also stressed the large $uncertainties associated with so far limited systematic efforts to investigate tipping across models. TIPMIP aims to close this gap by addressing tipping points across domains. Therefore, understanding the dynamics of tipping systems and associated risks is crucial for developing effective strategies to mitigate and adapt to the impacts of global environmental change. It has been identified as a topic of high interest for many IPCC member states and is subject of a dedicated expert meeting before the first AR7 lead author meeting.
recxXfc0Cj4ft3dRi.Expected Impacts: The opportunity will allow to evaluate key large scale tipping elements such as ice-sheet collapse, permafrost carbon release, tropical forest dieback and weakening of the Atlantic meridional ocean circulation as well as possible feedbacks associated with each individual tipping element. Outputs will be used to evaluate the uncertainties associated with identifying the existence of tipping points in the biogeophysical Earth system; the critical thresholds and temperature/warming levels which may induce tipping; as well as the interactions and feedbacks between (possible) tipping elements. Outputs may be then used by impact models and other end-user groups to evaluate the downstream consequences of tipping in the Earth system on human society.
recxXfc0Cj4ft3dRi.Justification of Resources: Almost all variables proposed for TIPMIP comply with standard Earth system modeling output, and serve two major purposes: (1) Analysing ESMs with respect to tipping points across all protocols. (2) Serving as forcing input for uncoupled/offline component models (e.g. standalone ice sheet models) in follow-up tailored tipping experiments. There is a strong overlap between TIPMIP variables and existing baseline variables, minimising additional computational costs while providing the base for a cross-domain analysis of tipping points.
recxXfc0Cj4ft3dRi.Technical Notes: TipMIP set of experiments will  be added once available on this system.  See https://github.com/WCRP-CMIP/CMIP6Plus_CVs/issues/78
recxXfc0Cj4ft3dRi.Title of Opportunity: Robust Risk Assessment of Tipping Points

recyH1unMjjUnOXW0.Description: These variables are needed to benchmark, understand, and attribute changes to the global carbon cycle, as well as other biogeochemical cycles on land and ocean.
recyH1unMjjUnOXW0.Expected Impacts: Understanding changes to carbon sinks across global change scenarios, and benchmarking the fidelity of land and ocean biogeochemical components of ESMs, is needed to understand the relationship between CO2 emissions, CO2 concentrations, global climate change, and other biogeochemical cycles, across historical, future, and idealized scenarios.
recyH1unMjjUnOXW0.Justification of Resources: The coupling of carbon and climate as enabled through Earth system models requires benchmarking the fidelity of carbon and other biogeochemical cycles, and attributing changes in carbon sinks to forcings and feedbacks in the Earth system.
recyH1unMjjUnOXW0.Title of Opportunity: Benchmarking and Attributing Changes to Global Carbon and other Biogeochemical Cycles

reczl0rTSLt1hfi2N.Description: These variables were requested to support studies focused on the impacts of climate change on the aviation sector. Climate change causes changes on the jet streams that in turn affect wind shear and can cause clear air turbulence as shown in multiple studies (https://doi.org/10.1038/nclimate1866, https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-23630-8\_23, https://doi.org/10.1017/aer.2021.109). The variables in this group allow to diagnose clear air turbulence that is of relevance for passenger safety concerns as well as planning of flight routes and times.
reczl0rTSLt1hfi2N.Expected Impacts: Climate change causes changes on the jet streams that in turn affect wind shear and can cause clear air turbulence as shown in multiple studies (https://doi.org/10.1038/nclimate1866, https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-23630-8\_23, https://doi.org/10.1017/aer.2021.109). The variables in this group allow to diagnose clear air turbulence that is of relevance for passenger safety concerns as well as planning of flight routes and times.
reczl0rTSLt1hfi2N.Justification of Resources: This request comprises a subset of 3 to 5 of the 27 pressure levels of standard variables (temperature, wind components) that can also be used for jet stream diagnostics and other dynamical studies.
reczl0rTSLt1hfi2N.Title of Opportunity: Impacts of climate change on aviation

rec35AnF2ytyNyHtE.Description: The phrase "integral\_wrt\_X\_of\_Y" means int Y dX. The abbreviation "wrt" means "with respect to". To specify the limits of the integral the data variable should have an axis for X and associated coordinate bounds. If no axis for X is associated with the data variable, or no coordinate bounds are specified, it is assumed that the integral is calculated over the entire vertical extent of the medium, e.g, if the medium is air the integral is assumed to be calculated over the full depth of the atmosphere. Conservative Temperature is defined as part of the Thermodynamic Equation of Seawater 2010 (TEOS-10) which was adopted in 2010 by the International Oceanographic Commission (IOC). Conservative Temperature is specific potential enthalpy (which has the standard name sea\_water\_specific\_potential\_enthalpy) divided by a fixed value of the specific heat capacity of sea water, namely cp\_0 = 3991.86795711963 J kg-1 K-1. The zero Joule reference temperature, referred to as bigthetao, is zero degrees Celsius. Conservative Temperature is a more accurate measure of the "heat content" of sea water, by a factor of one hundred, than is potential temperature. Because of this, it can be regarded as being proportional to the heat content of sea water per unit mass. Reference: [www.teos-10.org](http://www.teos-10.org); McDougall, 2003 doi: 10.1175/1520-0485(2003)033<0945:PEACOV>2.0.CO;2. The phrase "expressed\_as\_heat\_content" means that this quantity is calculated as the specific heat capacity times density of sea water multiplied by the conservative temperature of the sea water in the grid cell and integrated over depth.
rec35AnF2ytyNyHtE.Name: chcint
rec35AnF2ytyNyHtE.Title: integral wrt depth of sea water conservative temperature expressed as heat content

rec5hhjZWMo6P8SaT.Description: The phrase "integral\_wrt\_X\_of\_Y" means int Y dX. To specify the limits of the integral the data variable should have an axis for X and associated coordinate bounds. If no axis for X is associated with the data variable, or no coordinate bounds are specified, it is assumed that the integral is calculated over the entire vertical extent of the medium, e.g, if the medium is air the integral is assumed to be calculated over the full depth of the atmosphere. The abbreviation "wrt" means "with respect to". Depth is the vertical distance below the surface. Preformed Salinity, S\*, is defined as part of the Thermodynamic Equation of Seawater 2010 (TEOS-10) which was adopted in 2010 by the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC). Preformed Salinity is a salinity variable that is designed to be as conservative as possible, by removing the estimated biogeochemical influences on the sea water composition. Preformed Salinity is Absolute Salinity, S\_A (which has the standard name sea\_water\_absolute\_salinity), minus all contributions to sea water composition from biogeochemical processes. Preformed Salinity is the mass fraction of dissolved material in sea water. Reference: [www.teos-10.org](http://www.teos-10.org); Pawlowicz et al., 2011 doi: 10.5194/os-7-363-2011; Wright et al., 2011 doi: 10.5194/os-7-1-2011. There are also standard names for the precisely defined salinity quantities sea\_water\_knudsen\_salinity, S\_K (used for salinity observations between 1901 and 1966), sea\_water\_cox\_salinity, S\_C (used for salinity observations between 1967 and 1977), sea\_water\_practical\_salinity, S\_P (used for salinity observations from 1978 onwards), and sea\_water\_reference\_salinity. Salinity quantities that do not match any of the precise definitions should be given the more general standard name of sea\_water\_salinity.
rec5hhjZWMo6P8SaT.Name: pfscint
rec5hhjZWMo6P8SaT.Title: Integral wrt depth of sea water preformed salinity expressed as salt mass content

recH8tHGiTm7VL1mk.Description: The phrase "integral\_wrt\_X\_of\_Y" means int Y dX. To specify the limits of the integral the data variable should have an axis for X and associated coordinate bounds. If no axis for X is associated with the data variable, or no coordinate bounds are specified, it is assumed that the integral is calculated over the entire vertical extent of the medium, e.g, if the medium is air the integral is assumed to be calculated over the full depth of the atmosphere. The abbreviation "wrt" means "with respect to". Depth is the vertical distance below the surface. Absolute Salinity, S\_A, is defined as part of the Thermodynamic Equation of Seawater 2010 (TEOS-10) which was adopted in 2010 by the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC). It is the mass fraction of dissolved material in sea water. Absolute Salinity incorporates the spatial variations in the composition of sea water. This type of Absolute Salinity is also called "Density Salinity". TEOS-10 estimates Absolute Salinity as the salinity variable that, when used with the TEOS-10 expression for density, yields the correct density of a sea water sample even when the sample is not of Reference Composition. In practice, Absolute Salinity is often calculated from Practical Salinity using a spatial lookup table of pre-defined values of the Absolute Salinity Anomaly. It is recommended that the version of (TEOS-10) software and the associated Absolute Salinity Anomaly climatology be specified within metadata by attaching a comment attribute to the data variable. Reference: [www.teos-10.org](http://www.teos-10.org); Millero et al., 2008 doi: 10.1016/j.dsr.2007.10.001. There are also standard names for the precisely defined salinity quantities sea\_water\_knudsen\_salinity, S\_K (used for salinity observations between 1901 and 1966), sea\_water\_cox\_salinity, S\_C (used for salinity observations between 1967 and 1977), sea\_water\_practical\_salinity, S\_P (used for salinity observations from 1978 onwards), sea\_water\_preformed\_salinity, S\_\*, and sea\_water\_reference\_salinity. Salinity quantities that do not match any of the precise definitions should be given the more general standard name of sea\_water\_salinity.
recH8tHGiTm7VL1mk.Name: absscint
recH8tHGiTm7VL1mk.Title: Integral wrt depth of sea water absolute salinity expressed as salt mass content

The precise distinction between "fine" and "coarse" is model dependent. "Surface litter" means the part of the litter resting above the soil surface. The sum of the quantities with standard names wood\_debris\_mass\_content\_of\_nitrogen, surface\_litter\_mass\_content\_of\_nitrogen and subsurface\_litter\_mass\_content\_of\_nitrogen is the total nitrogen mass content of dead plant material.

recLpBTdQqpy2l1Mg.Description: Total RH of shrubs in the grid cell

recLpBTdQqpy2l1Mg.Title: Heterotrophic Respiration on Shrub Tiles as Carbon Mass Flux [kgC m-2 s-1]

recLpaNA9yZymrp0W.Description: Basal temperature that is used to force the ice sheet models, it is the temperature AT ice shelf-ocean interface.  Cell\_methods: area: mean where floating\_ice\_shelf
recLpaNA9yZymrp0W.Name: litempbotfl
recLpaNA9yZymrp0W.Title: Basal Temperature of Floating Ice Shelf

recLrtyeic7OkbXna.Description: NOy is the sum of all simulated oxidized nitrogen species out of NO, NO2, HNO3, HNO4, NO3 aerosol, NO3(radical), N2O5, PAN, other organic nitrates. Dry deposition includes gravitational settling and turbulent deposition.
recLrtyeic7OkbXna.Name: drynoy
recLrtyeic7OkbXna.Title: Dry Deposition Rate of NOy

recLwHpHiy7ICkof1.Name: fgco2
recLwHpHiy7ICkof1.Title: Surface Downward Mass Flux of Carbon as CO2 [kgC m-2 s-1]

recLxeNdhn3o9pIlf.Description: Tendency of salt content for a grid cell from parameterized submesoscale eddy advection.
recLxeNdhn3o9pIlf.Name: osaltpsmadvect
recLxeNdhn3o9pIlf.Title: Tendency of Sea Water Salinity Expressed as Salt Content Due to Parameterized Submesoscale Advection

recLzZVVg81lDzCRU.Description: Net heat conduction flux at the ice surface, i.e. the conductive heat flux from the centre of the uppermost vertical sea-ice grid box to the surface of the sea ice (energy flow per sea ice area). Positive for a downward heat flux.
recLzZVVg81lDzCRU.Name: siflcondtop
recLzZVVg81lDzCRU.Processing Comment: CHANGE SINCE CMIP6 in Title and Description - CMIP6:Net Conductive Heat Flux in Ice at the Surface CMIP7:Net Conductive Heat Flux in Sea Ice at the Surface
recLzZVVg81lDzCRU.Title: Net Conductive Heat Flux in Sea Ice at the Surface

recM2lO50NQOpE3P7.Description: The surface called "surface" means the lower boundary of the atmosphere. "Upward" indicates a vector component which is positive when directed upward (negative downward). In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics. The phrase "expressed\_as" is used in the construction A\_expressed\_as\_B, where B is a chemical constituent of A. It means that the quantity indicated by the standard name is calculated solely with respect to the B contained in A, neglecting all other chemical constituents of A. "Nox" means a combination of two radical species containing nitrogen and oxygen NO+NO2. "Vegetation" means any living plants e.g. trees, shrubs, grass. "Litter" is dead plant material in or above the soil.
recM2lO50NQOpE3P7.Name: fNOx
recM2lO50NQOpE3P7.Title: Total Land NOx Flux

recM3S9o2wgZ4rpLW.Name: rhVgt
recM3S9o2wgZ4rpLW.Title: Heterotrophic Respiration on Vegetation type as Carbon Mass Flux [kgC m-2 s-1]

recM6aVB2oW1v3qEe.Description: Tendency of heat content for a grid cell from parameterized mesoscale eddy diffusion. Reported only for models that use conservative temperature as prognostic field.
recM6aVB2oW1v3qEe.Name: ocontemppmdiff
recM6aVB2oW1v3qEe.Title: Tendency of Sea Water Conservative Temperature Expressed as Heat Content Due to Parameterized Mesoscale Diffusion

recMAZ6RB1VEzpJdI.Description: Deposition rate of sulfur dioxide due to wet processes
recMAZ6RB1VEzpJdI.Name: wetso2
recMAZ6RB1VEzpJdI.Title: Wet Deposition Rate of SO2

recMHndq4FzIASvA6.Description: This is the percentage of the entire grid cell that is covered by broadleaf deciduous trees.
recMHndq4FzIASvA6.Name: treeFracBdlDcd
recMHndq4FzIASvA6.Title: Broadleaf Deciduous Tree Area Percentage

recMM0kM3EznrTFCQ.Description: The mass per unit area (summed over all model layers) of frozen water.
recMM0kM3EznrTFCQ.Name: mrfso
recMM0kM3EznrTFCQ.Title: Soil Frozen Water Content

recMWYlip5jejD4qs.Description: Downwelling shortwave flux underneath sea ice, i.e. the amount of shortwave radiation that penetrates the sea ice and reaches the sea ice-ocean interface (energy flow per sea ice area). Always positive or zero.
recMWYlip5jejD4qs.Name: siflswdbot
recMWYlip5jejD4qs.Processing Comment: CHANGE SINCE CMIP6 in Title and Description - CMIP6: Downwelling Shortwave Flux Under Sea Ice, CMIP7: Downwelling Shortwave Flux under Sea Ice
recMWYlip5jejD4qs.Title: Downwelling Shortwave Flux under Sea Ice

recMXxEdWGpsaOTeJ.Description: This is requested only for the emission-driven coupled carbon climate model runs. This is the prescribed anthropogenic CO2 flux from fossil fuel use, including cement production, and flaring (but not from land-use changes, agricultural burning, forest regrowth, etc.)
recMXxEdWGpsaOTeJ.Name: fco2fos
recMXxEdWGpsaOTeJ.Title: Carbon Mass Flux into Atmosphere Due to Fossil Fuel Emissions of CO2 [kgC m-2 s-1]

recMiYTeeW6vlFLHh.Description: The surface called "surface" means the lower boundary of the atmosphere. "longwave" means longwave radiation. Downwelling radiation is radiation from above. It does not mean "net downward". When thought of as being incident on a surface, a radiative flux is sometimes called "irradiance". In addition, it is identical with the quantity measured by a cosine-collector light-meter and sometimes called "vector irradiance". In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics.
recMiYTeeW6vlFLHh.Name: rlds
recMiYTeeW6vlFLHh.Title: Surface Downwelling Longwave Radiation

recMj2PBP9Jx51vMB.Description: Mole fraction is used in the construction mole\_fraction\_of\_X\_in\_Y, where X is a material constituent of Y.  A chemical species denoted by X may be described by a single term such as 'nitrogen' or a phrase such as 'nox\_expressed\_as\_nitrogen'. The chemical formula for HCFC22 is CHClF2.  The IUPAC name for HCFC22 is chloro-difluoro-methane.
recMj2PBP9Jx51vMB.Name: hcfc22global
recMj2PBP9Jx51vMB.Title: Global Mean Mole Fraction of HCFC22

recMpYM49THZJQ7gW.Description: Joint probability distribution function, giving probability of cloud as a function of optical thickness and particle size, as measured by MODIS. For cloud ice particles.
recMpYM49THZJQ7gW.Name: jpdftaureicemodis
recMpYM49THZJQ7gW.Processing Comment: CHANGE: Standard name changed to clarify definition
recMpYM49THZJQ7gW.Title: MODIS Joint Distribution of Optical Thickness and Particle Size, Ice-Topped

recMxRjXjIlbz1mzg.Description: Tendency of salt content for a grid cell from all processes.
recMxRjXjIlbz1mzg.Name: osalttend
recMxRjXjIlbz1mzg.Title: Tendency of Sea Water Salinity Expressed as Salt Content

recN0bW5SfAFRNitJ.Description: In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics.   'Sinking' is the gravitational settling of particulate matter suspended in a liquid. A sinking flux is positive downwards and is calculated relative to the movement of the surrounding fluid.
recN0bW5SfAFRNitJ.Name: epn100
recN0bW5SfAFRNitJ.Title: Downward Flux of Particulate Nitrogen

recN2hGSHrSWAV5tB.Description: In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics.  The specification of a physical process by the phrase due\_to\_process means that the quantity named is a  single term in a sum of terms which together compose the general quantity  named by omitting the phrase.  " Iceberg thermodynamics" refers to the addition or subtraction of mass due to surface and basal fluxes, i.e., due to melting, sublimation and fusion.
recN2hGSHrSWAV5tB.Name: hfibthermds
recN2hGSHrSWAV5tB.Title: Heat Flux into Sea Water Due to Iceberg Thermodynamics

recN51dZilGofzu8G.Description: Tendency of Air Temperature due to Clear Sky Longwave Radiative Heating
recN51dZilGofzu8G.Name: tntrlcs
recN51dZilGofzu8G.Title: Tendency of Air Temperature Due to Clear Sky Longwave Radiative Heating

recNEaNBCRD8hinwU.Name: snicemIs
recNEaNBCRD8hinwU.Title: Ice Sheet Surface Snow and Ice Melt Flux

recNFxB8nD12ciqzD.Description: Calculated in the absence of clouds.
recNFxB8nD12ciqzD.Name: rsutcs
recNFxB8nD12ciqzD.Title: TOA Outgoing Clear-Sky Shortwave Radiation

recNILFoYxlqpFcyK.Description: carbon from the diatom phytoplankton component concentration alone

recNIxZVBhMhI7JEP.Description: Mass flux of water due to irrigation.
recNIxZVBhMhI7JEP.Name: irrLut
recNIxZVBhMhI7JEP.Title: Irrigation Flux Including any Irrigation for Crops, Trees, Pasture, or Urban Lawns

recNLLuKxjIlCKGf9.Description: Total aerosol AOD due to dust aerosol at a wavelength of 550 nanometres.
recNLLuKxjIlCKGf9.Name: od550dust
recNLLuKxjIlCKGf9.Title: Dust Optical Thickness at 550nm

recNMjev9XjuAknd5.Description: Vegetation height averaged over the shrub fraction of a grid cell.

recNMjev9XjuAknd5.Title: Height of Shrubs

recNU8X1Yosua7Ny7.Description: Y-component of the atmospheric stress on the surface of sea ice divided by grid-cell area.
recNU8X1Yosua7Ny7.Name: sistrydtop
recNU8X1Yosua7Ny7.Title: Y-Component of Atmospheric Stress on Sea Ice

recNcjP3MZcOC4DQK.Description: Downward northward wind stress at the surface
recNcjP3MZcOC4DQK.Name: tauv

recO4uSewkpeUETdb.Name: emico
recO4uSewkpeUETdb.Title: Total Emission Rate of CO

recO6dtEbqeIMLuqw.Description: Wave period associated with the most energetic waves in total wave spectrum, incorporating both wind-sea and swell waves. In spectral wind wave models, this represents the spectral peak across the entire two-dimensional wave spectrum, incorporating both wind-sea and swell waves.
recO6dtEbqeIMLuqw.Name: wpp
recO6dtEbqeIMLuqw.Title: Total Wave Peak Period

recO9vCQXomFZmiCE.Description: This is the percentage of the entire grid cell that is covered by broadleaf evergreen trees.
recO9vCQXomFZmiCE.Name: treeFracBdlEvg
recO9vCQXomFZmiCE.Title: Broadleaf Evergreen Tree Area Percentage

recOA4eBcDmQusyz1.Description: Contributions to heat transport from parameterized eddy-induced advective transport due to any subgrid advective process. Diagnosed here as a function of latitude and basin.  Use Celsius for temperature scale.

recOFiM1nGh8TRouS.Description: Joint probability distribution function, giving probability of cloud as a function of optical thickness and particle size, as measured by MODIS. For liquid cloud particles.

recOLoWcnNUklO494.Description: "shortwave" means shortwave radiation. "Layer" means any layer with upper and lower boundaries that have constant values in some vertical coordinate. There must be a vertical coordinate variable indicating the extent of the layer(s). If the layers are model layers, the vertical coordinate can be model\_level\_number, but it is recommended to specify a physical coordinate (in a scalar or auxiliary coordinate variable) as well. Net absorbed radiation is the difference between absorbed and emitted radiation.
recOLoWcnNUklO494.Name: rsdoabsorb
recOLoWcnNUklO494.Title: Net Rate of Absorption of Shortwave Energy in Ocean Layer

recOMvdCBv6Z9N1i3.Description: Mass flux of surface meltwater which refreezes within the snowpack. Computed as the total refreezing on the land ice portion of the grid cell divided by land ice area in the grid cell.
recOMvdCBv6Z9N1i3.Name: snicefreez
recOMvdCBv6Z9N1i3.Title: Surface Snow and Ice Refreeze Flux

recONkK1RA6nLVtNc.Description: Net (sum of transport in all directions) sea ice mass transport through the following four passages, positive into the Arctic Ocean. Note that the definitions of the passages are for SIMIP purposes just meant as default values as given by the physical ocean MIP described in Griffies et al. (2016). Individual models might chose slightly different definitions as given by their grid geometry. 1. Fram Strait: (11.5W,81.3N) to (10.5E,79.6N). 2. Canadian Arctic Archipelago: (128.2W,70.6N) to (59.3W,82.1N). 3. Barents Sea Opening: (16.8E,76.5N) to (19.2E,70.2N). 4. Bering Strait: (171W,66.2N) to (166W,65N).
recONkK1RA6nLVtNc.Name: simassacrossline
recONkK1RA6nLVtNc.Processing Comment: CHANGE SINCE CMIP6 in Title and Description - CMIP6: Sea Mass Area Flux Through Straits, CMIP7: Sea-Ice Mass Flux Through Straits
recONkK1RA6nLVtNc.Title: Sea-Ice Mass Flux Through Straits

recOPoKzdmf8cbeWT.Description: The rate of synthesis of carbon-14 in biomass from inorganic precursors by autotrophs ("producers") expressed as the mass of carbon which it contains. For example, photosynthesis in plants or phytoplankton. The producers also respire some of this biomass and the difference is referred to as the net primary production.
recOPoKzdmf8cbeWT.Name: gppc14
recOPoKzdmf8cbeWT.Title: Carbon-14 Mass Flux out of Atmosphere Due to Gross Primary Production on Land [kgC m-2 s-1]

recOYQ5bdzJV510lk.Description: Change in ice algal carbon mass due to photosynthesis per sea ice unit area per unit time.
recOYQ5bdzJV510lk.Name: sigpp
recOYQ5bdzJV510lk.Title: Gross Primary Productivity in Sea Ice as Carbon Amount Flux

recObEi6H2QzO4HHI.Description: Total integrated area of sea ice in the Southern Hemisphere (where siconc > 0). Does not include grid cells partially covered by land.
recObEi6H2QzO4HHI.Name: siareas
recObEi6H2QzO4HHI.Title: Sea-Ice Area South

recOhuP4g8IiBVSLR.Name: expfeob
recOhuP4g8IiBVSLR.Title: Sinking Flux of Particulate Iron Reaching the Ocean Bottom

recOjWybBQswxoIxL.Description: Rate of change of sea-ice mass through lateral melting/dissolution divided by grid-cell area (report zero if not explicitly calculated thermodynamically). Always negative or zero.
recOjWybBQswxoIxL.Name: sidmassmeltlat
recOjWybBQswxoIxL.Processing Comment: CHANGE SINCE CMIP6 in Name and Title - CMIP6:sidmasslat and Lateral Sea Ice Melt Rate CMIP7:sidmassmeltlat and Sea-Ice Mass Change Through Lateral Melting
recOjWybBQswxoIxL.Title: Sea-Ice Mass Change Through Lateral Melting

recOqZsfzUq7kVBPX.Description: Average height of the highest one-third of waves present in the sea state, incorporating just wind-sea waves (i.e., local wind waves). It is derived from the wind-sea wave spectrum using spectral moments. Specifically, this parameter is four times the square root of the integral over all directions and all frequencies of the two-dimensional wind-sea wave spectrum.
recOqZsfzUq7kVBPX.Name: swhwindsea
recOqZsfzUq7kVBPX.Title: Wind Sea Significant Wave Height

recP0RlKt0dvMyB2B.Description: Total grazing of phytoplankton by zooplankton defined as tendency of moles of carbon per cubic metre.
recP0RlKt0dvMyB2B.Name: graz

recP5LAIOEPpVbuwU.Description: The total dry mass of nitrate aerosol particles per unit area.

recP5LAIOEPpVbuwU.Title: Load of NO3

recP5PU6Ijtlz5DFd.Name: hus6
recP5PU6Ijtlz5DFd.Title: Specific humidity for global field (6 pressure level)

recPA2k5zHHyEjKrl.Description: The total mass of liquid water in cloud per unit area.

recPA2k5zHHyEjKrl.Title: Liquid Water Path

Note that the definitions of the passages are for SIMIP purposes just meant as default values as given by the physical ocean MIP described in Griffies et al. (2016). Individual models might chose slightly different definitions as given by their grid geometry. 1. Fram Strait: (11.5W,81.3N) to (10.5E,79.6N). 2. recPILVnwOHIFNl4z.Name: siareaacrossline
recPILVnwOHIFNl4z.Title: Sea-Ice Area Flux Through Straits

recPS8aj19bkvAojr.Description: carbon concentration from the picophytoplankton (<2 um) component alone
recPS8aj19bkvAojr.Name: phypicoos
recPS8aj19bkvAojr.Title: Surface Mole Concentration of Picophytoplankton Expressed as Carbon in Sea Water

recPV387QnNHnftcz.Description: Net latent heat flux over sea ice (energy flow per sea ice area). Positive for a downward heat flux.
recPV387QnNHnftcz.Name: sifllattop
recPV387QnNHnftcz.Processing Comment: CHANGE SINCE CMIP6 in Name and CF Standard Name and Description - CMIP6:sifllatstop and surface_upward_latent_heat_flux CMIP7:sifllattop and surface_downward_latent_heat_flux
recPV387QnNHnftcz.Title: Net Latent Heat Flux over Sea Ice

recPa9fhwEJ7QlvhD.Description: Flux of CO2 from product pools into the atmosphere. recPcI3Mf1mjEdpVd.Description: Percentage of each grid cell that is occupied by snow that rests on land portion of cell.

recPfEFVqniipb3l9.Description: Downward flux of particulate organic carbon
recPfEFVqniipb3l9.Name: expc
recPfEFVqniipb3l9.Title: Downward Flux of Particulate Organic Carbon

recPlXOg9ccc41smj.Name: abs550ss
recPlXOg9ccc41smj.Title: Ambient Seasalt Aerosol Absorption Optical Thickness at 550nm

recPtCfbY2LRS370i.Description: Rate of change of sea-ice mass due to sea ice formation in supercooled water (often through frazil formation) divided by grid-cell area. Always positive or zero.
recPtCfbY2LRS370i.Name: sidmassgrowthwat
recPtCfbY2LRS370i.Title: Sea-Ice Mass Change Through Growth in Supercooled Open Water (Frazil)

recPy6Ek6v7Bjehnv.Description: Vertical/dianeutral diffusivity applied to prognostic temperature field.
recPy6Ek6v7Bjehnv.Name: difvho
recPy6Ek6v7Bjehnv.Title: Ocean Vertical Heat Diffusivity

recPzfd5r0mLgpde2.Description: Top-of-atmosphere outgoing longwave radiation calculated using carbon dioxide concentrations increased fourfold

recQ8X47we1jcEBuL.Description: The phrase "change\_over\_time\_in\_X" means change in a quantity X over a time-interval, which should be defined by the bounds of the time coordinate. "Canopy" means the plant or vegetation canopy. Canopy water is the water on the canopy. "Water" means water in all phases, including frozen, i.e. ice and snow. "Amount" means mass per unit area.

recQ9aAPNaX1l2vra.Description: Average height of the highest one-third of waves present in the sea state, incorporating both wind-sea and swell waves. This is a key parameter for describing wave energy and is derived from the wave spectrum using spectral moments. Specifically, this parameter is four times the square root of the integral over all directions and all frequencies of the two-dimensional wave spectrum.
recQ9aAPNaX1l2vra.Name: swh
recQ9aAPNaX1l2vra.Title: Total Significant Wave Height

recQ9xMkJepAp2YWS.Description:
The effective dynamic sea level as if sea ice (and snow) at a grid cell were converted to liquid seawater.  The liquid-water equivalent sea surface which the liquid would have if the ice were replaced by an equal mass of sea water of the density of the surface water in its vicinity. Inverse barometer responses from sea-ice (and snow) loading are removed using equation H3 of Griffies et al, 2016 (<https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-9-3231-2016>). zos is a dynamic sea level should have zero global area mean.
Ocean dynamic sea level is defined by Gregory et al. (2019: [doi.org/10.1007/s10712-019-09525-z](doi.org/10.1007/s10712-019-09525-z) )
recQ9xMkJepAp2YWS.Name: zos
recQ9xMkJepAp2YWS.Title: Sea Surface Height Above Geoid

Square of temperature of liquid ocean.

recSrPagERQlOcK7Q.Title: Age of Sea Ice

recSv8ZcIaGJp2unb.Title: Total Plant Nitrogen Uptake (Sum of Ammonium and Nitrate) Irrespective of the Source of Nitrogen

For example any diffusive mixing by the boundary layer scheme would be included.

The sum of the quantities with standard names mass\_flux\_of\_carbon\_into\_litter\_from\_vegetation\_due\_to\_mortality and mass\_flux\_of\_carbon\_into\_litter\_from\_vegetation\_due\_to\_senescence is mass\_flux\_of\_carbon\_into\_litter\_from\_vegetation.

recTs2YM9d9rwSmxK.Description: carbon concentration from the diazotrophic phytoplankton component alone

recViDY1o6MB1eKz6.Description:
Sea water salinity is the salt content of sea water, often on the Practical Salinity Scale of 1978. However, the unqualified term 'salinity' is generic and does not necessarily imply any particular method of calculation. The units of salinity are dimensionless and the units attribute should normally be given as 1e-3 or 0.001 i.e. parts per thousand. 
Evaluated at the upper boundary of the liquid ocean, including at the lower boundary of sea-ice and floating ice shelves.
recViDY1o6MB1eKz6.Name: sosga
recViDY1o6MB1eKz6.Processing Comment: CHANGE SINCE CMIP6 in Units - CMIP6:1 CMIP7:1E-03

recVmeW9xSb7TheIm.Description: End of year values (not annual mean); note that percentage should be reported as percentage of land grid cell (example: frac\_lnd = 0.5, frac\_ocn = 0.5, frac\_crop\_lnd = 0.2 (of land portion of grid cell), then frac\_lut(crop) = 0.5\*0.2 = 0.1)
recVmeW9xSb7TheIm.Name: fracLut
recVmeW9xSb7TheIm.Title: Percentage of Grid Cell for Each Land-Use Tile

recVn13JyW8I8cuse.Description: Mean height of sea-ice surface (i.e. snow-ice interface when snow covered) above sea level. This follows the classical definition of freeboard for in situ observations. In the satellite community, sometimes the total height of sea ice and snow above sea level is referred to as freeboard. This can easily be calculated by adding sisnthick to sifb.
recVn13JyW8I8cuse.Name: sifb
recVn13JyW8I8cuse.Title: Sea-Ice Freeboard

recVqokT8Cmbrxpkl.Description: Concentration 'as seen from space' over ice-cloud portion of grid cell.  This is the value from uppermost model layer with ice cloud or, if available, it is the sum over all ice cloud tops, no matter where they occur, as long as they are seen from the top of the atmosphere. Weight by total ice cloud top fraction (as seen from TOA) of each time sample when computing monthly mean.
recVqokT8Cmbrxpkl.Name: cldnci
recVqokT8Cmbrxpkl.Title: Ice Crystal Number Concentration of Cloud Tops

recW4Op4nmYMVRYV3.Description: Areal fraction of a given grid cell that is covered by sea ice on the atmosphere grid, independent of the thickness of that ice.
recW4Op4nmYMVRYV3.Name: siconca
recW4Op4nmYMVRYV3.Processing Comment: CHANGE SINCE CMIP6 in Title and Units and Description - CMIP6:Sea-Ice Area Percentage (Atmospheric Grid) and % CMIP7:Sea-Ice Area Fraction (Atmospheric Grid) and 1
recW4Op4nmYMVRYV3.Title: Sea-Ice Area Percentage (Atmospheric Grid)

recW6saTQ8Gs7gQB2.Description: Tendency of heat content for a grid cell from parameterized eddy advection (any form of eddy advection). Reported only for models that use conservative temperature as prognostic field.

recWHtminK7fcTazx.Description: Total area of the floating ice shelves (the component of ice sheet that flows over ocean)

recWN8t0lEjU79lAJ.Name: exparagob
recWN8t0lEjU79lAJ.Title: Sinking Flux of Aragonite Reaching the Ocean Bottom

recWSmRg6Z3ibypMF.Description: Rate of change of sea-ice mass through melting at the ice surface divided by grid-cell area. This number is independent of the actual fate of the meltwater, and will hence include all sea-ice meltwater that drains into the ocean and all sea-ice meltwater that is collected by a melt-pond parameterisation. Always negative or zero.

recWSmRg6Z3ibypMF.Title: Sea-Ice Mass Change Through Surface Melting

recWTwi2G7i0y6qGb.Description: Downwelling longwave flux from the atmosphere to the sea-ice surface (energy flow per sea ice area). Always positive or zero.
recWTwi2G7i0y6qGb.Name: sifllwdtop
recWTwi2G7i0y6qGb.Title: Downwelling Longwave Flux over Sea Ice

recWZUMtHnI2QAL44.Description: Mole fraction is used in the construction mole\_fraction\_of\_X\_in\_Y, where X is a material constituent of Y.

recWZUMtHnI2QAL44.Title: O3 Volume Mixing Ratio in Lowest Model Layer

recWeyGhm9zrHEQKC.Name: tropch4loss
recWeyGhm9zrHEQKC.Title: Tropospheric loss of CH4 from chemical destruction

recWhEnF7xcbNIC0m.Description: Phytoplankton are algae that grow where there is sufficient light to support photosynthesis. "Miscellaneous phytoplankton" are all those phytoplankton that are not diatoms, diazotrophs, calcareous phytoplankton, picophytoplankton or other separately named components of the phytoplankton population. "Iron growth limitation" means the ratio of the growth rate of a species population in the environment (where there is a finite availability of iron) to the theoretical growth rate if there were no such limit on iron availability.
recWhEnF7xcbNIC0m.Name: limfemisc
recWhEnF7xcbNIC0m.Title: Iron Limitation of Other Phytoplankton

recWrHKn098n8TOWb.Description: The surface called "surface" means the lower boundary of the atmosphere. "longwave" means longwave radiation. Upwelling radiation is radiation from below. It does not mean "net upward". When thought of as being incident on a surface, a radiative flux is sometimes called "irradiance". In addition, it is identical with the quantity measured by a cosine-collector light-meter and sometimes called "vector irradiance". In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics.
recWrHKn098n8TOWb.Name: rlusIs
recWrHKn098n8TOWb.Title: Ice Sheet Surface Upwelling Longwave Radiation

recWuxROsSjpvQOWM.Description: Overturning mass streamfunction arising from all advective mass transport processes, resolved and parameterized.
recWuxROsSjpvQOWM.Name: msftyz

recWuxROsSjpvQOWM.Title: Ocean Y Overturning Mass Streamfunction

recWviMlOkCwd4jhS.Description: Northward component of the near surface wind
recWviMlOkCwd4jhS.Name: vas
recWviMlOkCwd4jhS.Title: Northward Near-Surface Wind

recWyc6n8emhLNYK1.Description: Chlorophyll from diatom phytoplankton component concentration alone
recWyc6n8emhLNYK1.Name: chldiat
recWyc6n8emhLNYK1.Title: Mass Concentration of Diatoms Expressed as Chlorophyll in Sea Water

recWyu71xooVy8Nz9.Description: The rate of synthesis of biomass from inorganic precursors by autotrophs ("producers") expressed as the mass of carbon which it contains. For example, photosynthesis in plants or phytoplankton. The producers also respire some of this biomass and the difference is referred to as the net primary production.
recWyu71xooVy8Nz9.Name: gpp
recWyu71xooVy8Nz9.Title: Carbon Mass Flux out of Atmosphere Due to Gross Primary Production on Land [kgC m-2 s-1]

recX2EPT8u1OFxDEO.Description: X-component of the atmospheric stress on the surface of sea ice divided by grid-cell area.
recX2EPT8u1OFxDEO.Name: sistrxdtop
recX2EPT8u1OFxDEO.Title: X-Component of Atmospheric Stress on Sea Ice

recX36TrKl8muEOO3.Description: Mass flux of water from the soil layer into ground water.
recX36TrKl8muEOO3.Name: qgwr
recX36TrKl8muEOO3.Title: Groundwater Recharge from Soil Layer

recX9hNt5oj7wlF9F.Description: carbon concentration from the picophytoplankton (<2 um) component alone

recX9hNt5oj7wlF9F.Title: Mole Concentration of Picophytoplankton Expressed as Carbon in Sea Water

recXAuM5FzNwDVTD0.Description: Simulated reflectance from PARASOL as seen at the top of the atmosphere for 5 solar zenith angles. Valid only over ocean and for one viewing direction (viewing zenith angle of 30 degrees and relative azimuth angle 320 degrees).
recXAuM5FzNwDVTD0.Name: parasolRefl
recXAuM5FzNwDVTD0.Title: PARASOL Reflectance

recXDivacivQyXDpo.Description: Depth-integrated total heat transport from resolved and parameterized processes across different lines on the Earth's surface (based on appendix J and table J1 of Griffies et al., 2016). Formally, this means the integral along the line of the normal component of the heat transport. Positive and negative numbers refer to total northward/eastward and southward/westward transports, respectively. The transport should be evaluated for the full depth of the ocean, except for the Pacific Equatorial Undercurrent, which is averaged from the surface to 350m. Use Celsius for temperature scale.
recXDivacivQyXDpo.Name: hfacrossline
recXDivacivQyXDpo.Title: Ocean Heat Transport across Lines

recXDrVYZgJQE5fVD.Description: Percentage of area covered by vegetation.
recXDrVYZgJQE5fVD.Name: cnc
recXDrVYZgJQE5fVD.Title: Canopy Covered Area Percentage

recXJsMBpgdIFV4UA.Title: Nitrogen Mass in Litter Pool

recXJzEYOUI1MWDJw.Description: In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics. The atmosphere convective mass flux is the vertical transport of mass for a field of cumulus clouds or thermals, given by the product of air density and vertical velocity. For an area-average, cell\_methods should specify whether the average is over all the area or the area of updrafts only.
recXJzEYOUI1MWDJw.Name: mcu
recXJzEYOUI1MWDJw.Title: Convective Updraft Mass Flux

recXLKgqAlkmOqdZA.Description: Total NPP of shrubs in the grid cell

recXU7gbb2Kb0DzP9.Description: minimum boundary layer height during the day (add cell\_methods attribute: "time: minimum")

recXUJU5h6D8axkbT.Description: Percentage of entire grid cell  that is covered by C4 PFTs (including grass and crops).

recXUJU5h6D8axkbT.Title: Percentage Cover by C4 Plant Functional Type

This flux should be reproducible by differencing the sum of all carbon pools (cVeg, cLitter, cSoil, and cProducts or equivalently cLand) from one time step to the next, except in the case of lateral transfer of carbon due to harvest, riverine transport of dissolved organic and/or inorganic carbon, or any other process (in which case the lateral\_carbon\_transfer\_over\_land term, see below, will be zero data).

recXh8l4wBTA365es.Description: Vertically integrated primary (organic carbon) production by phytoplankton based on nitrate uptake alone

recY3fxH3oXd9jXAh.Description: The surface called "surface" means the lower boundary of the atmosphere. "shortwave" means shortwave radiation. Upwelling radiation is radiation from below. It does not mean "net upward". When thought of as being incident on a surface, a radiative flux is sometimes called "irradiance". In addition, it is identical with the quantity measured by a cosine-collector light-meter and sometimes called "vector irradiance". In accordance with common usage in geophysical disciplines, "flux" implies per unit area, called "flux density" in physics.

recYFSrbJcNvtf9A4.Description: Diatoms are phytoplankton with an external skeleton made of silica. Phytoplankton are algae that grow where there is sufficient light to support photosynthesis. "Nitrogen growth limitation" means the ratio of the growth rate of a species population in the environment (where there is a finite availability of nitrogen) to the theoretical growth rate if there were no such limit on nitrogen availability.
recYFSrbJcNvtf9A4.Name: limndiat
recYFSrbJcNvtf9A4.Title: Nitrogen Limitation of Diatoms

recYHPoczKnIe47f0.Description: Areal fraction of a given grid cell that is covered by sea ice on the ocean grid, independent of the thickness of that ice.

recYHPoczKnIe47f0.Title: Sea-Ice Area Percentage (Ocean Grid)

recaHeRxSH9pMrlZ5.Description: The phrase "integral\_wrt\_X\_of\_Y" means int Y dX. To specify the limits of the integral the data variable should have an axis for X and associated coordinate bounds. If no axis for X is associated with the data variable, or no coordinate bounds are specified, it is assumed that the integral is calculated over the entire vertical extent of the medium, e.g, if the medium is air the integral is assumed to be calculated over the full depth of the atmosphere. The abbreviation "wrt" means "with respect to". Depth is the vertical distance below the surface. Practical Salinity, S\_P, is a determination of the salinity of sea water, based on its electrical conductance. The measured conductance, corrected for temperature and pressure, is compared to the conductance of a standard potassium chloride solution, producing a value on the Practical Salinity Scale of 1978 (PSS-78). This name should not be used to describe salinity observations made before 1978, or ones not based on conductance measurements. Conversion of Practical Salinity to other precisely defined salinity measures should use the appropriate formulas specified by TEOS-10. Other standard names for precisely defined salinity quantities are sea\_water\_absolute\_salinity (S\_A); sea\_water\_preformed\_salinity (S\_\*), sea\_water\_reference\_salinity (S\_R); sea\_water\_cox\_salinity (S\_C), used for salinity observations between 1967 and 1977; and sea\_water\_knudsen\_salinity (S\_K), used for salinity observations between 1901 and 1966. Salinity quantities that do not match any of the precise definitions shoul d be given the more general standard name of sea\_water\_salinity. Reference: [www.teos-10.org](http://www.teos-10.org); Lewis, 1980 doi:10.1109/JOE.1980.1145448.
recaHeRxSH9pMrlZ5.Name: scint
recaHeRxSH9pMrlZ5.Title: Integral wrt depth of sea water practical salinity expressed as salt mass content
